newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Five dead, thousands flee in Indonesia riot.
newsitem.headline: Five dead, thousands flee in Indonesia riot.

text.p: At least five people were killed and thousands forced to flee to safety during tribal rioting this week, sparked by a fight over a woman in Indonesia's West Kalimantan province, media and officials said on Friday.
The Jakarta Post newspaper said the riot in Sanggau Ledo was sparked on Monday by a brawl between two groups of youths over a woman during a concert.
It said five people were killed, nine injured and "countless" houses burned in the violence which continued through Thursday and included arson and looting.
About 3,250 people have fled 100 km (60 miles) from the riot area in Sanggau Ledo District to the coastal town of Singkawang.

The official Antara news agency quoted Kalimantan's military commander, Major-General Namoeri Anoem, as saying on Thursday that thousands of people had also been evacuated by air force planes to Pontianak, the provincial capital.
A policeman in Singkawang told Reuters by telephone on Friday the situation was under control, but he refused to give further details.
"It's safe now, but I can't give you other comment," he said.
Local military officials also declined to comment.

The Jakarta Post said the trouble erupted during a folk show after a man from Madura island off the main island of Java reportedly stabbed two Dayak tribesmen in the stomach. The Dayaks are natives of Kalimantan province on Borneo island.
The paper said that by Thursday, thousands of people were on a burning and looting rampage.
An employee of the state-owned telecommunication company in Singkawang told Reuters a curfew was still in place on Friday and there was no telephone connection to Sanggau Ledo.
Antara quoted the Kalimantan military commander as saying six youths had been arrested on suspicion of starting the disturbances.

Last week, a mob of mainly Moslem youths set buildings and churches ablaze in the West Java town of Tasikmalaya, apparently incensed by a report of police brutality towards some Moslem religious teachers.
Four people died and 15 were injured in those riots.
